bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Extensive industry experience: over 50 years executing large and complex infrastructure projects in India and overseas, with proven delivery in challenging terrain such as Jammu & Kashmir and the Northeast.
- End-to-end 'Concept to Commissioning' execution capability supported by in-house design across civil, mechanical, electrical and signalling disciplines, with a dedicated Design and Development Cell and a new tunnel design vertical.
- Tunnelling pioneer: more than 200 trained tunnel engineers and over 100 km of tunnel mining completed in challenging Himalayan geology, including the 12.75 km USBRL tunnel, the longest transportation tunnel in the country.
- Market leadership in railway electrification: more than 11,567 TKM of electrification executed in India and abroad over four decades.
- Institutional credibility as a Navratna CPSE under the Ministry of Railways, with government backing helping navigate land acquisition, clearances and stakeholder issues.
- Diversified portfolio across railways, highways, buildings, metro rail and renewable energy in domestic and international markets, reducing single-segment dependence.
- Established domestic and international footprint: 408 domestic and 131 international projects delivered across 25 countries.
- Healthy financial position with a debt-free standalone balance sheet, strong liquidity and a consistent track record of dividend payments since inception.
- Asset-light operating model using strategic outsourcing and subcontracting for efficient capital utilisation and improved return on capital, while owning its own construction equipment for complex work.
- Centralised procurement for major items securing competitive rates, with 50-60 percent of procurement carried out in-house on EPC projects.
- External recognition: the only Indian PSU in ENR's 2025 top 250 International Contractors and top 250 Global Contractors lists; ranked 242nd in the 2025 Fortune India 500; rated 'Very Good' under the MoU with the Ministry of Railways for FY 2024-25.
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Thin operating margins inherent to competitively bid government EPC work — MD&A Weaknesses: the EPC business is characterised by intense competition and competitive bidding, particularly in government infrastructure projects, resulting in relatively low operating margins; limited pricing flexibility and exposure to cost escalations leave a narrow cushion against execution risks.
- Order-book contraction and loss of nomination-based awards — MD&A Threats and Future Outlook: the Ministry of Railways ended nomination-based awards so IRCON must now compete with other PSUs and private companies; management states the order book position has reduced due to higher competition and that stiff competition and margin reduction while securing new jobs is expected to continue.
- Working-capital intensity and receivable/collection risk — MD&A Weaknesses: long project execution cycles and milestone-based payment structures require significant working capital; delays in work certification, client approvals, milestone payments and receivable collections can adversely impact cash conversion, operating cash flows and capital efficiency.
- Land acquisition, clearance and regulatory delays causing time and cost overruns — MD&A Threats and Risk Management: infrastructure projects are susceptible to delays from land acquisition, environmental clearances and local political opposition; in the Indian context IRCON specifically faces non-availability of encumbrance-free land and delays in approval of drawings and estimates, posing risks of time and cost overruns that are often uncompensated by the client.
- Contractual, claims and arbitration exposure — MD&A Threats: claims, arbitration, project delays and client disputes may impact earnings and cash flows; project timelines are frequently susceptible to site clearance delays and slow conversion of order inflows into revenue.
- Commodity price volatility on fixed-price contracts — MD&A Threats: sharp fluctuations in prices of steel, cement and fuel can significantly impact project costs, especially for fixed-price contracts, squeezing margins; mitigated partly through price escalation clauses in contracts.
- Geopolitical and foreign-exchange exposure on overseas operations — MD&A Weaknesses and Threats: overseas operations expose the Company to political instability, changes in government policies and regulatory frameworks, cross-border regulatory shifts, currency fluctuations and diplomatic relations in countries where it operates, which may affect project execution and financial performance.
- Operational constraints and reduced flexibility from PSU status and government policy dependence — MD&A Weaknesses and Threats: as a PSU, IRCON must comply with statutory regulations, public procurement norms and administrative procedures more rigorous than private peers, which may limit operational flexibility and slow decision-making; a change in government or shift in economic priorities could lead to a slowdown in work orders and profitability.

business.body:
- "Navratna Central Public Sector Enterprise (CPSE) under the Ministry of Railways"; the deck's journey timeline runs 1976 (established under the Companies Act), 1992 (converted into Public Limited Company), 1998 (granted "Miniratna" status), 2006 (Schedule "A" Company), 2018 (equity shares listed on NSE & BSE), 2020 (achieved turnover of Rs.5,000 crore), 2023 (turnover crossed Rs.10,000 crore), 2023 (upgraded to "Navratna" Company) and 2024 (highest ever turnover achieved).
- Track record cited as 408 Domestic and 131 International under "Projects Completed", alongside executed work of 5,858 TKM railway track, 10,762 RKM railway electrification, 7,258 KMS roads and highways, 1.59 Mn Sqm buildings, 167 KMS tunnel and 183 Nos. bridges.

business.body: IRCON is a turnkey infrastructure contractor that executes projects on an Engineering, Procurement and Construction (EPC) basis, alongside Project Management Consultancy, Public Private Partnership concessions and real estate development. It builds and maintains railways and rail bridges, highways, metro and high-speed rail, tunnels, railway electrification and EHV sub-stations, signalling and telecommunication systems, railway production units and station buildings, with in-house design, civil, mechanical, electrical and S&T capability from concept to commissioning. Its customers are almost entirely government agencies — the Ministry of Railways, NHAI, NHSRCL, Chennai Metro Rail, DFCCIL, Airports Authority of India, RLDA, NCRTC and DMRC in India, plus overseas clients in Algeria, Sri Lanka, Bangladesh, Malaysia and Myanmar.
business.title: What they do

business.body:
- **Railways:** New broad-gauge railway lines and doubling, Rail bridges and rail-cum-road bridges, Railway tunnels (NATM), Yard remodelling and station redevelopment, Railway production units and coach manufacturing facilities, Diesel and electric loco shed upgradation, Rolling stock export, leasing and maintenance
- **Railway Electrification & Electrical:** 25 kV railway electrification (OHE, ROCS, FOCS), HT grid and traction sub-stations up to 400 kV, Extra High Tension transmission lines and EHV cabling, Gas Insulated Sub-stations and transmission lines up to 220 kV, Tunnel ventilation, safety and electro-mechanical works, Grid-connected solar power plants
- **Signal & Telecom:** Electronic Interlocking, Automatic Block Signalling, KAVACH / Station Kavach (TCAS) and Kavach telecom towers, Automatic Train Protection and Centralized Traffic Control, Remote Diagnostics & Predictive Maintenance System, Integrated Passenger Information Systems, Integrated Tunnel Communication System
- **Highways:** Highways, expressways and four/six-laning, Road bridges, ROBs, flyovers and road tunnels, BOT / toll and annuity highway concessions through SPVs
- **Metro & Urban Transit:** Metro ballasted and ballastless track, Metro traction, power supply, SCADA, E&M, lifts and escalators, Regional Rapid Transit System traction and power supply
- **Buildings & Other:** Commercial, institutional and residential buildings and townships, Hospitals, museums, university campuses and schools, Multi-Functional Complexes and station buildings, Industrial civil and structural works (e.g. petrochemical plant civil works), Hydro-electric project civil works
- **Services:** Project Management Consultancy, Real estate development, construction and leasing of office and commercial realty

outlook.title: Guidance / outlook

outlook.body: The company's growth optionality is linked to the growth of the infrastructure sector in India, with a focus on railways and construction projects.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Diversify across industry segments through 'new engines of growth' while continuing to focus on the railway sector, so as to hedge against risks concentrated in particular industry sectors and limited geographical regions.
- Expand into high-growth adjacent infrastructure segments leveraging core EPC expertise — renewable energy, metro rail, KAVACH (Automatic Train Protection), water infrastructure and transmission.
- Enhance the project portfolio in both domestic and international markets to achieve a healthy order book and profit margins.
- Pursue international growth in Algeria, Uganda and other African nations, in South Asia (Sri Lanka, Bangladesh, Nepal), and evaluate prospects in Southeast Asian markets.
- Use strategic MOUs, alliances and joint ventures — including PPP partnerships with private players — to enter new markets and participate in larger, more complex projects.
- Pursue selective bidding, cost optimisation, efficient execution and effective contract management to defend margins in a competitively bid EPC market.
- Strengthen working capital management through close monitoring of receivables, timely billing, proactive stakeholder engagement and efficient cash flow planning.
- Maintain an asset-light operating model through strategic outsourcing and subcontracting to improve capital utilisation and return on capital.
- Grow the real estate and commercial operations business over the medium and long term through the Estate Management Department, shifting from a pure construction company to a project development and operation company.
- Build in-house capability further, notably a dedicated Tunnel Design / Underground Structures vertical in the Design and Development Cell.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: IRCON's expansion is project-execution rather than plant-building: it is executing a 500 MW grid-connected solar power plant under the MNRE CPSU Scheme, of which 250 MW was commissioned in FY 2025-26 in three phases of 75+75+100 MW and synchronised to the Southern Grid for sale of power to South Western Railway, taking cumulative commissioned solar capacity to 400 MW of the 500 MW targeted, with the balance targeted to be connected shortly; on full commissioning approximately 1,076 million units will be supplied annually. In railway electrification it is executing more than 2,700 RKM of works and 29 traction sub-stations under the Ministry of Railways' 'Mission 100% Railway Electrification', of which more than 2,693 RKM and 22 traction sub-stations have been commissioned along with about 200 km of 132 kV transmission lines. Tunnelling and new-line build-out continues on the Sivok-Rangpo rail link connecting Sikkim, where 12 of 14 tunnels have been completed by NATM and about 38.6 km of electro-mechanical works in tunnels T-1 to T-14 are under execution, following completion of the 12.75 km USBRL tunnel, the longest transportation tunnel in the country. Urban-transit build-out includes two MMRDA contracts for traction, power supply, SCADA and E&M works on Mumbai Metro Line-5 (about 13 km) and Line-6 (about 15.6 km), where design, procurement and execution are under way, and a 220 kV D/C transmission line from Koradi-II to Mankapur sub-station for MSETCL under execution. The Company has established a dedicated new vertical for Tunnel Design and Underground Structures within its in-house Design and Development Cell to build capacity, and has set up an Estate Management Department to grow the real estate business over the medium and long term through plot development, building construction and leasing or sale of immovable properties. Capacity built earlier includes the fully integrated stainless steel coach manufacturing facility at Raebareli, which converts rolled steel sheets into finished coaches and includes a shell fabrication line, robotic-welding bogie shop, wheel shop, paint shop, automated material storage and retrieval and a 3 MW solar park. Internationally, IRCON is pursuing opportunities in Algeria, Uganda and other African nations, in Sri Lanka, Bangladesh and Nepal, and is evaluating prospects in Southeast Asian markets.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Government infrastructure spending is the primary demand driver: the Union Budget 2026-27 increased the capital outlay for infrastructure to Rs 12.2 lakh crore from Rs 11.21 lakh crore in the previous year.
- Record railway capex underpins the core market: the Union Budget 2026-27 earmarked a record CAPEX of Rs 2.78 lakh crore for Indian Railways, and announced development of seven high-speed rail corridors.
- Sustained programme pipeline from the National Infrastructure Pipeline, PM Gati Shakti, Bharatmala Pariyojana, National Logistics Policy and railway modernisation is expected to generate significant opportunities across transportation, logistics and urban infrastructure.
- Long-run infrastructure investment: per CRISIL's Infrastructure Yearbook 2023, India is expected to invest nearly Rs 143 lakh crore in infrastructure through FY2030, more than double the prior seven-year period.
- Urbanisation demand: per the World Bank, nearly 600 million people are expected to reside in urban areas by 2036, creating substantial demand for rail, roads, urban transit and logistics infrastructure.
- Renewable energy opportunity from the Government's target of 500 GW of non-fossil fuel installed capacity by 2030, which IRCON expects to address through its subsidiary and related infrastructure projects.
- Growing adoption of the PPP model and liberalised FDI (100% under the automatic route in railway infrastructure) is expected to broaden participation in larger projects.
- Margin headwind from the shift away from nomination-based awards: management states it has had stiff competition and margin reduction while securing new jobs and that this challenge is expected to continue.
- Revenue decline in FY 2025-26 is attributed to the successful completion of some major projects and stagnation in the order book, with reduced turnover and provisioning in ongoing projects hitting profit.
- Receivables stretch attributed by management to the transition in the order book from nomination-based projects to competitive bidding, along with changes in client payment terms.
- Management expects steady growth in the business in the long run despite a reduced order book position, citing experience, expertise, technological capability and a sound financial position.
- Macro backdrop: real GDP is estimated to have grown 7.7% in FY 2025-26 with RBI projecting 6.6% for FY 2026-27, while global growth is projected at 3.0% for 2026, with geopolitical tension, commodity volatility and supply chain disruption cited as downside risks.
- IRCON's order book as on March 31, 2026 stood at Rs 24,984.47 Crore, with Rs 19,459.35 Crore of work in the Railways sector and Rs 3,918.97 Crore in the Highway sector.
- Of the total order book, Rs 13,458.87 Crore of work was secured through competitive bidding and Rs 11,525.60 Crore through nomination basis.
- Management describes the order book as stagnant/reduced, citing higher competition, and says the Company is trying its level best to enhance the order book position and maintain its margins.
- The Ministry of Railways revoked the policy of competition amongst railway PSUs in October 2021 and introduced open tendering for awarding railway works, so IRCON now competes with other PSUs and private companies.
- The Business Development Department secured 15 projects during FY 2025-26, spanning rail bridges, KAVACH signalling, metro electrical packages, hydro civil works, schools and a petrochemical civil package.
- The S&T new business development vertical booked orders worth approximately Rs 900 Crore in FY 2025-26, including station Kavach works, telecom towers for Kavach, EI with auto signalling, predictive maintenance of signalling gear and integrated tunnel communication.
- International projects contributed Rs 296.24 Crore, or 3.49% of operating turnover, in FY 2025-26 versus Rs 339.10 Crore (3.33%) in the prior year.

Capacity built earlier includes the fully integrated stainless steel coach manufacturing facility at Raebareli, which converts rolled steel sheets into finished coaches and includes a shell fabrication line, robotic-welding bogie shop, wheel shop, paint shop, automated material storage and retrieval and a 3 MW solar park. one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: IRCON is a Navratna Central Public Sector Undertaking under the Ministry of Railways and an integrated engineering and construction company specialising in major transportation infrastructure, with an order book of Rs 24,984.47 Crore as on March 31, 2026.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: IRCON is a turnkey infrastructure contractor that executes projects on an Engineering, Procurement and Construction (EPC) basis, alongside Project Management Consultancy, Public Private Partnership concessions and real estate development. It builds and maintains railways and rail bridges, highways, metro and high-speed rail, tunnels, railway electrification and EHV sub-stations, signalling and telecommunication systems, railway production units and station buildings, with in-house design, civil, mechanical, electrical and S&T capability from concept to commissioning. Its customers are almost entirely government agencies — the Ministry of Railways, NHAI, NHSRCL, Chennai Metro Rail, DFCCIL, Airports Authority of India, RLDA, NCRTC and DMRC in India, plus overseas clients in Algeria, Sri Lanka, Bangladesh, Malaysia and Myanmar.

group_structure.title: Group structure (profile)
group_structure.body:
- Ircon Infrastructure & Services Limited (IISL / IrconISL) — subsidiary: Wholly owned subsidiary, 100% held; delivers Project Management Consultancy work in the infrastructure sector. Acquired 30.09.2009. Does not participate in the listed entity's Business Responsibility initiatives.
- Ircon Shivpuri Guna Tollway Limited (ISGTL) — subsidiary: Wholly owned subsidiary, 100% held; Shivpuri-Guna highway toll project SPV. Acquired 12.05.2015.

- Ircon Davanagere Haveri Highway Limited (IDHHL) — subsidiary: Wholly owned subsidiary, 100% held; Davanagere-Haveri highway project SPV. Acquired 11.05.2017.
- Ircon Vadodara Kim Expressway Limited (IVKEL) — subsidiary: Wholly owned subsidiary, 100% held; Vadodara-Kim expressway project SPV. Acquired 16.05.2018.

- Ircon Renewable Power Limited (IRPL) — subsidiary: Subsidiary; renewable energy vehicle through which IRCON pursues solar power opportunities. Acquired 13.01.2022.
- Ircon Akloli Shirsad Expressway Limited (ASEL) — subsidiary: Subsidiary; expressway project SPV. Acquired 23.12.2021.
- Ircon Ludhiana Rupnagar Highway Limited (ILRHL) — subsidiary: Subsidiary; Ludhiana-Rupnagar highway project SPV. Acquired 24.12.2021.
- Ircon Bhoj Morbe Expressway Limited (IBMEL) — subsidiary: Wholly owned subsidiary; SPV for the eight-lane access-controlled expressway in the Bhoj-Morbe section, a spur of the Vadodara-Mumbai Expressway in Maharashtra under Bharatmala Pariyojna Phase-II Package-XVII, and has awarded that EPC contract back to IRCON. Acquired 06.01.2022.
- Ircon Haridwar Bypass Limited (IHBL) — subsidiary: Wholly owned subsidiary; SPV for upgradation and four-laning of Haridwar Bypass Package-1 in Uttarakhand, and has awarded that EPC contract back to IRCON. Acquired 13.01.2022.
- Chhattisgarh East Railway Limited (CERL) — JV: Joint venture company; has awarded IRCON execution of the East Corridor Rail Project in Chhattisgarh under a Project Execution Agreement dated 18.01.2014, running until the railway corridor becomes operational in line with the Concession Agreement. IRCON is paid actual cost of work plus a specified percentage towards overheads and profit.
- Chhattisgarh East-West Railway Limited (CEWRL) — JV: Joint venture company; has awarded IRCON execution of the East-West Corridor Rail Project in Chhattisgarh under a Project Execution Agreement dated 05.04.2014, running until the railway corridor becomes operational. IRCON is paid actual cost of work plus a specified percentage towards overheads and profit.
- Mahanadi Coal Railway Limited (MCRL) — JV: Joint venture company; related-party arrangement covering award of work for preparation of feasibility/project work. IRCON directors hold nominee positions on its board.
- Jharkhand Central Railway Limited (JCRL) — JV: Rail infrastructure joint venture; IRCON functional directors serve as part-time nominee directors. Associated with the Shivpur-Kathautia coal rail connectivity project in Jharkhand.
- Indian Railway Stations Development Corporation Limited — related party: Company in which an IRCON functional director serves as a part-time nominee director and chairs its Audit Committee.
- Jharkhand Rail Infrastructure Development Corporation Limited — related party: Company in which an IRCON Government Nominee Director serves as Government Nominee Director.
- Ministry of Railways / Rail Land Development Authority (RLDA) — related party: Promoter-group counterparties; the BRSR notes that sales to related parties include a substantial share of total sales from the Ministry of Railways and RLDA.

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:
- **Railways:** New broad-gauge railway lines and doubling, Rail bridges and rail-cum-road bridges, Railway tunnels (NATM), Yard remodelling and station redevelopment, Railway production units and coach manufacturing facilities, Diesel and electric loco shed upgradation, Rolling stock export, leasing and maintenance
- **Railway Electrification & Electrical:** 25 kV railway electrification (OHE, ROCS, FOCS), HT grid and traction sub-stations up to 400 kV, Extra High Tension transmission lines and EHV cabling, Gas Insulated Sub-stations and transmission lines up to 220 kV, Tunnel ventilation, safety and electro-mechanical works, Grid-connected solar power plants

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Government infrastructure spending is the primary demand driver: the Union Budget 2026-27 increased the capital outlay for infrastructure to Rs 12.2 lakh crore from Rs 11.21 lakh crore in the previous year.
- Record railway capex underpins the core market: the Union Budget 2026-27 earmarked a record CAPEX of Rs 2.78 lakh crore for Indian Railways, and announced development of seven high-speed rail corridors.
- Sustained programme pipeline from the National Infrastructure Pipeline, PM Gati Shakti, Bharatmala Pariyojana, National Logistics Policy and railway modernisation is expected to generate significant opportunities across transportation, logistics and urban infrastructure.
- Long-run infrastructure investment: per CRISIL's Infrastructure Yearbook 2023, India is expected to invest nearly Rs 143 lakh crore in infrastructure through FY2030, more than double the prior seven-year period.
- Urbanisation demand: per the World Bank, nearly 600 million people are expected to reside in urban areas by 2036, creating substantial demand for rail, roads, urban transit and logistics infrastructure.
- Renewable energy opportunity from the Government's target of 500 GW of non-fossil fuel installed capacity by 2030, which IRCON expects to address through its subsidiary and related infrastructure projects.
- Growing adoption of the PPP model and liberalised FDI (100% under the automatic route in railway infrastructure) is expected to broaden participation in larger projects.
- Margin headwind from the shift away from nomination-based awards: management states it has had stiff competition and margin reduction while securing new jobs and that this challenge is expected to continue.
- Revenue decline in FY 2025-26 is attributed to the successful completion of some major projects and stagnation in the order book, with reduced turnover and provisioning in ongoing projects hitting profit.
- Receivables stretch attributed by management to the transition in the order book from nomination-based projects to competitive bidding, along with changes in client payment terms.
- Management expects steady growth in the business in the long run despite a reduced order book position, citing experience, expertise, technological capability and a sound financial position.
- Macro backdrop: real GDP is estimated to have grown 7.7% in FY 2025-26 with RBI projecting 6.6% for FY 2026-27, while global growth is projected at 3.0% for 2026, with geopolitical tension, commodity volatility and supply chain disruption cited as downside risks.
- IRCON's order book as on March 31, 2026 stood at Rs 24,984.47 Crore, with Rs 19,459.35 Crore of work in the Railways sector and Rs 3,918.97 Crore in the Highway sector.
- Of the total order book, Rs 13,458.87 Crore of work was secured through competitive bidding and Rs 11,525.60 Crore through nomination basis.
- Management describes the order book as stagnant/reduced, citing higher competition, and says the Company is trying its level best to enhance the order book position and maintain its margins.
- The Ministry of Railways revoked the policy of competition amongst railway PSUs in October 2021 and introduced open tendering for awarding railway works, so IRCON now competes with other PSUs and private companies.
- The Business Development Department secured 15 projects during FY 2025-26, spanning rail bridges, KAVACH signalling, metro electrical packages, hydro civil works, schools and a petrochemical civil package.
- The S&T new business development vertical booked orders worth approximately Rs 900 Crore in FY 2025-26, including station Kavach works, telecom towers for Kavach, EI with auto signalling, predictive maintenance of signalling gear and integrated tunnel communication.
- International projects contributed Rs 296.24 Crore, or 3.49% of operating turnover, in FY 2025-26 versus Rs 339.10 Crore (3.33%) in the prior year.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: IRCON's expansion is project-execution rather than plant-building: it is executing a 500 MW grid-connected solar power plant under the MNRE CPSU Scheme, of which 250 MW was commissioned in FY 2025-26 in three phases of 75+75+100 MW and synchronised to the Southern Grid for sale of power to South Western Railway, taking cumulative commissioned solar capacity to 400 MW of the 500 MW targeted, with the balance targeted to be connected shortly; on full commissioning approximately 1,076 million units will be supplied annually. In railway electrification it is executing more than 2,700 RKM of works and 29 traction sub-stations under the Ministry of Railways' 'Mission 100% Railway Electrification', of which more than 2,693 RKM and 22 traction sub-stations have been commissioned along with about 200 km of 132 kV transmission lines. Tunnelling and new-line build-out continues on the Sivok-Rangpo rail link connecting Sikkim, where 12 of 14 tunnels have been completed by NATM and about 38.6 km of electro-mechanical works in tunnels T-1 to T-14 are under execution, following completion of the 12.75 km USBRL tunnel, the longest transportation tunnel in the country. Urban-transit build-out includes two MMRDA contracts for traction, power supply, SCADA and E&M works on Mumbai Metro Line-5 (about 13 km) and Line-6 (about 15.6 km), where design, procurement and execution are under way, and a 220 kV D/C transmission line from Koradi-II to Mankapur sub-station for MSETCL under execution. The Company has established a dedicated new vertical for Tunnel Design and Underground Structures within its in-house Design and Development Cell to build capacity, and has set up an Estate Management Department to grow the real estate business over the medium and long term through plot development, building construction and leasing or sale of immovable properties. Capacity built earlier includes the fully integrated stainless steel coach manufacturing facility at Raebareli, which converts rolled steel sheets into finished coaches and includes a shell fabrication line, robotic-welding bogie shop, wheel shop, paint shop, automated material storage and retrieval and a 3 MW solar park. Internationally, IRCON is pursuing opportunities in Algeria, Uganda and other African nations, in Sri Lanka, Bangladesh and Nepal, and is evaluating prospects in Southeast Asian markets.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Extensive industry experience: over 50 years executing large and complex infrastructure projects in India and overseas, with proven delivery in challenging terrain such as Jammu & Kashmir and the Northeast.
- End-to-end 'Concept to Commissioning' execution capability supported by in-house design across civil, mechanical, electrical and signalling disciplines, with a dedicated Design and Development Cell and a new tunnel design vertical.
- Tunnelling pioneer: more than 200 trained tunnel engineers and over 100 km of tunnel mining completed in challenging Himalayan geology, including the 12.75 km USBRL tunnel, the longest transportation tunnel in the country.
- Market leadership in railway electrification: more than 11,567 TKM of electrification executed in India and abroad over four decades.
- Institutional credibility as a Navratna CPSE under the Ministry of Railways, with government backing helping navigate land acquisition, clearances and stakeholder issues.
- Diversified portfolio across railways, highways, buildings, metro rail and renewable energy in domestic and international markets, reducing single-segment dependence.
- Established domestic and international footprint: 408 domestic and 131 international projects delivered across 25 countries.
- Healthy financial position with a debt-free standalone balance sheet, strong liquidity and a consistent track record of dividend payments since inception.
- Asset-light operating model using strategic outsourcing and subcontracting for efficient capital utilisation and improved return on capital, while owning its own construction equipment for complex work.
- Centralised procurement for major items securing competitive rates, with 50-60 percent of procurement carried out in-house on EPC projects.
- External recognition: the only Indian PSU in ENR's 2025 top 250 International Contractors and top 250 Global Contractors lists; ranked 242nd in the 2025 Fortune India 500; rated 'Very Good' under the MoU with the Ministry of Railways for FY 2024-25.
